# BMS / DJMax keysound-slicer UX audit

## Evidence boundaries
This is a source-led audit. Where a page is a guide or wiki, the finding is attributed to that author rather than presented as a universal product fact. I found no usable Sayaslicer Discussions content, no direct PTSEQUENCER manual, and no accessible YouTube comment body; those gaps are not filled by inference ([Discussions](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/discussions), [PTSEQUENCER secondary report](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)).

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Open/drag audio → place markers → set offset/snap → preview → copy BMSE/iBMSC data or export keysounds; supports MIDI-marker and Mid2BMS renamer imports ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) | Zero-cross can move markers and break iBMSC precision; BPM-change support is explicitly incomplete; export still renders files rather than maintaining a chart-linked virtual-slice model ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) | Snap 1/1–1/192; no documented max marker count ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) | WAV/keysound export plus BMSE base-62 toggle and iBMSC/BMSE clipboard ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) |
| **Woslicer II** | Drag WAV/OGG → BPM/offset → grid and markers with keyboard → preview → batch export → drag numbered WAVs into BMSE → clipboard-paste placements ([BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit), [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) | Many files make placement “a hard work”; WAV format/bit-depth failures can terminate it; tails need manual adjustment ([FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer)) | Documented tutorial says III supports up to 192 divisions/bar; no total-slice max found ([Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) | Numbered WAVs + BMSE clipboard; `.wos` save/reopen in the community notes ([BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)) |
| **Woslicer III** | Drag WAV → BPM, offset, fade, noise gate, grid → click cut points → WAV output and `.wos` save → BMSE definitions/sequence paste ([Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Batch output can appear disabled until filename field is populated; Explorer ordering and BMSE start slot can silently misnumber definitions; a technical investigation reports pop noise from its tail treatment ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)) | Grid max 192/bar; output numbering is normally `xxx_000.wav` and can exceed 3 digits; no total max documented ([Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) | Batch WAV, `.wos`, clipboard sequence ([Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)） |
| **BMHelper / Mid2BMS** | MIDI → split/reduce notes by pitch/length/velocity → render in DAW → pass cut positions to slicer → define and place in BMSE; BMHelper also generates MIDI/BMS arrangement data ([BMHelper](https://github.com/zardoru/bmhelper), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Keys­witch-heavy or automation-heavy material is a poor fit; Mid2BMS outputs can clutter the source folder; detailed current UI/limits were not available from the fetched Mid2BMS site ([atWiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/12.html), [trap.jp](https://trap.jp/post/777/), [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/)) | No documented slice max; Base62-modified BMHelper/Mid2BMS variants are reported, but compatibility must be tested ([Base62 note](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n5d30f5d703?hl=en)) | MIDI, cut-position clipboard, BMS sequence clipboard, rendered WAVs ([BMHelper](https://github.com/zardoru/bmhelper), [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)) |
| **dtinth/sound-slicer** | `.txt` + WAV → numbered slices + BMS clipboard; rhythmic mode slices every event, melodic mode groups by note/length/velocity and requires re-rendering ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | Rhythmic mode can produce 1,000 slices for 1,000 notes and slight gaps; both modes do not support BPM changes; melodic mode requires a DAW round trip ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | No max; no BPM-change support ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | WAV slices + clipboard data ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) |
| **FL Studio Fruity Slicer / Slicex** | Detect/fixed-grid/manual slices → piano-roll dump or drag regions to sampler; declick/zero-cross tools are available ([Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm), [Slicex manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Slicex.htm)) | Long-loop beat detection can be inaccurate; real-time declick cannot restore an already-short decay; users report difficulty moving from Fruity Slicer to Slicex time-stretch/groove workflows ([Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm), [forum](https://forum.image-line.com/viewtopic.php?t=188396)) | No BMS-specific max; fixed divisions, threshold, beat detection and zero-cross options ([Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm)) | Piano-roll notes, WAV/processed sample and groove export ([Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm)) |
| **PTSEQUENCER** | No primary manual was found. A secondary reference describes it as a DJMAX pattern tool and reports 1,023 historically, later 2,047, keysounds; treat as unverified until primary documentation is obtained ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)) | Workflow, settings and export behavior not verifiable from fetched primary sources ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)) | Reported 1,023/2,047 key-sound figures are secondary, not a verified tool limit ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%음)) | Not established |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline
- **P0 — timing is split across incompatible coordinate systems.** Woslicer requires BPM and offset, then markers are copied to BMSE; Sayaslicer can snap 1/1–1/192 but warns that zero-cross moves markers and can make iBMSC output fail. A single timeline should display milliseconds, source samples, beat/bar grid and target chart quantization simultaneously ([Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)).
- **P1 — BPM changes are a real gap.** sound-slicer explicitly supports no BPM changes; Sayaslicer calls better BPM-change support planned, including MIDI BPM import and proper grid display ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)).
- **P1 — alignment and tails require listening/manual correction.** Woslicer guides instruct users to tune offset against waveform and preview, while other guides say tails need adjustment; Woslicer III’s investigated reverse/invert tail can create a pop ([Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)).
- **P2 — no chart preview in the slicer.** The cited tools export clipboard/files for a separate editor rather than showing target notes over the waveform ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)). This is an observed workflow gap, not a claim that every version lacks any visualization.

### Interface
- **P0 — export ceremony and hidden state.** Users must move between BMHelper, DAW, Woslicer, Explorer and BMSE/iBMSC; Woslicer’s batch-output workaround involves clicking a black area to make a filename appear ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)). Replace this with one visible project state, explicit source/output paths, and a single “Import to Studio” transaction.
- **P1 — silent numbering errors.** Woslicer/BMSE numbering depends on starting slot, Explorer sort order and selection order; this can create incorrect definitions without an obvious error ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [FC2 guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)). Use stable slice IDs and a previewable mapping table instead of filenames as identity.
- **P1 — keyboard efficiency is valuable but discoverability is poor.** Woslicer II uses `Z/C/V/B/T/Y/M/P/Enter`; Sayaslicer adds marker selection, undo/redo, snap navigation and BMSE/iBMSC clipboard shortcuts. Keep command parity, searchable shortcuts and a visible keymap ([BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)).
- **P2 — format and platform friction.** Woslicer may fail on 24/32-bit WAVs and Sayaslicer’s macOS build is unsigned; normalize/import with an actionable diagnostic rather than a crash or OS gatekeeper surprise ([Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)).

### Settings
- **P0 — quantization vs audible quality is conflated.** Sayaslicer documents the conflict: zero-cross reduces clicks but moves markers and can break iBMSC precision; Woslicer III exposes fade, noise gate and grid, while BMSMaker3 users tune silence-cut thresholds to preserve reverb ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3), [BMSMaker3 note](https://note.com/soramizawakana/n/n98560efdc58d)). Settings need independent “audible boundary” and “chart timestamp,” with per-slice override and before/after preview.
- **P1 — no single safe tail policy.** Fade-before-cut shortens sound; fade-after-cut may leak the next sound; the Woslicer III investigation identifies a pop tradeoff ([Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)). Provide tail mode choices: hard, fade, preserve natural tail, reverse-tail compatibility, with warnings and waveform preview.
- **P1 — automation and keyswitches break the MIDI shortcut.** BMHelper is documented as unsuitable for heavy keyswitch/automation use, forcing manual rough slicing ([atWiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/12.html), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)). Provide audio-first slicing plus optional MIDI grouping, not a MIDI prerequisite.
- **P2 — normalization/format settings are under-documented.** The requested sources document fade, noise gate, zero-cross and silent-tail tools but do not establish a universal “Sensitivity 0.55” or Normalize setting for these BMS slicers; do not hard-code those as existing-tool facts ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)).

### Backend
- **P0 — destructive file explosion and identity loss.** Traditional flows render hundreds of numbered WAVs, then depend on Explorer order and editor slots; sound-slicer explicitly contrasts 1,000 events → 1,000 slices, while Woslicer docs describe numbered output and manual import ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)). Use `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` as stable identity and render only on finalize.
- **P0 — compatibility ceilings and overflow.** Classic BMS is documented at 1,295 definitions using base36 `01–ZZ`; BMSE/iBMSC workflows historically use that ceiling, while modified tools support base62 and report LR2 post-decode memory failures around 1.5 GB ([BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit), [editor notes](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/editors.html), [Base62 note](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n5d30f5d703?hl=en)). The product should count unique slices, warn before target overflow, and let users choose deduplication or compatibility export.
- **P1 — legacy voice stealing can truncate tails.** The keysound reference reports older same-lane playback cutting off the previous sample, while TECHNIKA 2-era playback is described as non-interfering ([key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)). Implement a target mode (BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA), voice-policy preview and conflict warnings rather than silently changing audio.
- **P1 — large-source robustness matters.** Sayaslicer issue #5 records very large files becoming laggy/unusable due to an audio-buffer integer overflow; the release says this was fixed, proving the class of failure is real ([issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5)). Stream/decode progressively, cache waveform levels, and never require all source samples in one integer-sized buffer.
- **P2 — round-trip is absent from legacy clipboard workflows.** Existing documented workflows end at clipboard paste/export; they do not establish a reversible slicer↔chart-editor link ([BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)). Store source range IDs in the Studio project and regenerate export artifacts deterministically.

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these
1. **Keyboard-first speed plus mouse/table navigation.** Sayaslicer preserves Woslicer-style shortcuts while adding marker-table jumping, selection, undo/redo and snap navigation ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)).
2. **Interchange breadth.** Keep BMSE clipboard, iBMSC export, optional BMSE base62, MIDI-marker import, Mid2BMS renamer arrays and keysound-list export ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)).
3. **Project persistence.** Save/load `.wos`-like work state and marker copy/paste so a long slicing session is recoverable ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)).
4. **Audible cleanup with explicit caveat.** Keep zero-cross, silent-tail threshold and fade, but expose the exact boundary movement and preserve chart timing separately ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)).
5. **Woslicer’s directness.** Drag an audio file, set BPM/offset/grid, click points, preview, batch export; this remains the fastest novice path ([Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)).

## 4. Top 10 recommendations, prioritized

1. **P0 — Make virtual slices the canonical model.** Store source URI/hash, start/end ms, chart time, target mode and per-slice processing; export WAV/OGG only at finalize. This directly removes the numbered-file/Explorer-order failure documented in Woslicer workflows ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)).
2. **P0 — Add a dual timeline.** Bottom: source waveform with ms/sample ruler; top: Studio chart preview with bars, beats, notes and playhead sync. Existing tools separate waveform slicing from BMSE/iBMSC chart placement, creating the handoff problem ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)).
3. **P0 — Make Import to Studio transactional and reversible.** One action creates notes linked to slice IDs, shows a mapping/conflict report, and permits Studio→Slicer edits without re-export/re-import ceremony. The need is evidenced by the multi-application clipboard workflow and filename-order hazards ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [editor notes](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/editors.html)).
4. **P0 — Separate chart timestamp from audio boundary.** Zero-cross/fade/tail processing may move audible boundaries; retain the exact chart time and show a before/after click-safe preview ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)).
5. **P1 — Implement deterministic 1/192 quantization plus BPM-map support.** Offer 1/4…1/192 presets, arbitrary snap, resnap-all, and piecewise BPM maps; do not claim full BPM support until grid and clipboard output both honor changes ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)).
6. **P1 — Add target modes and a voice-policy simulator.** BMS, RESPECT and TECHNIKA modes should show unique-key counts, lane conflicts, retrigger/steal behavior and tail truncation before export ([key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%E9%음)).
7. **P1 — Add a Slice Library and deduplication.** Show all virtual slices with waveform thumbnail, source range, chart uses, audible length, overrides and unique-count impact; allow reuse like sound-slicer’s 500-note/10-note example ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)).
8. **P1 — Make settings per-slice overrideable.** Global Sensitivity/threshold, zero-cross, fade, normalize and auto-advance should be defaults; each slice can override with a visible badge and A/B audition. This addresses documented tail, noise-gate and zero-cross tradeoffs ([Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)).
9. **P1 — Build compatibility validators.** Preflight audio bit depth/channel/format, filename/extension portability, BMS base36/base62 capacity, LR2 memory risk, and missing/long keysounds; provide actionable conversion, not a crash ([Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer), [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit), [Base62 note](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n5d30f5d703?hl=en)).
10. **P2 — Preserve expert shortcuts, add discoverability and recovery.** Keep Z/C/V/B/M/P/Enter-style operations, add command search, remapping, visible status, autosave, crash recovery and a keymap overlay; large-file issue #5 and Woslicer hidden filename state show why recovery/status matter ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)).

### Caveat on requested settings
The fetched sources substantiate BPM, offset, grid, fade, noise gate, zero-cross/silent-tail and snapping controls, but do **not** substantiate a universal existing-tool “Sensitivity 0.55”, Normalize, or Auto-advance Grid/Beat/Off setting. Those should be treated as DJMax Studio design proposals, not retrospective facts about the surveyed tools ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer), [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)).
